{{Short description|Military installation in the city of Johnston, Iowa}}
{{Use American English|date=July 2025}}
[[File:Human Statue of Liberty; 18,000 officers and men at Camp Dodge, Des Moines, Ia.; Col. Wm. Newman, commanding; Col. Rush S. Wells, directing LCCN2002699754.jpg|thumb|right|Human Statue of Liberty, created by [[Arthur Mole|Mole and Thomas]] using 18,000 officers and enlisted men at Camp Dodge near Des Moines, Iowa, 1918, during World War I]]
'''Camp Dodge''' is a military installation in the city of [[Johnston, Iowa]]. Centrally located near the capital of Iowa, it currently serves as the headquarters of the [[Iowa National Guard]].

== History ==
Original construction of the post began in 1907, to provide a place for the National Guard units to train.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=http://www.historian.itgo.com/camp.htm |title=Camp Dodge|website=www.historian.itgo.com}}</ref> In 1917, the installation was handed over to national authorities and greatly expanded to become a regional training center for forces to participate in the First World War.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/facility/camp-dodge.htm|title=Camp Dodge|website=www.globalsecurity.org}}</ref>

The name Camp Dodge comes from Brigadier General [[Grenville M. Dodge]], who organized Iowa's first National Guard unit in 1856.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iptv.org/iowapathways/mypath.cfm?ounid=ob_000264 |title=Grenville M. Dodge, An Iowa Hero |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100429193326/http://www.iptv.org/iowapathways/mypath.cfm?ounid=ob_000264 |archive-date=2010-04-29 }} Iowa Public Television site</ref>  Although not a native-born Iowan, he became a well-known figure and resided within the state for most of his adult life.  He is considered a War hero for his service and also served a term as a U.S. Congressman representing the state.

[[File:Camp Dodge Postcard 1918.jpg|thumb|A post card sent by an American enlisted man from Camp Dodge, IA around 1918]]

In June 1917, the 163rd Depot Brigade was formed at Camp Dodge.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://archive.org/details/thdivisioninwor00unkngoog|title=The 88th Division in the World War of 1914–1918|date=October 5, 1919|publisher=New York, Wynkoop Hallenbeck Crawford Company|via=Internet Archive}}</ref> The brigade was the base unit for the [[88th Infantry Division (United States)|88th Division]], which processed new draftees and provided basic training.<ref>The Brigade: Its Organization and Employment in the US Army: A History, John J. McGrath, Combat Studies Institute Press Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, 2004, p.35.</ref>  Later it appears the brigade despatched soldiers to multiple divisions, as two African American soldiers were sent to the 163rd Depot Brigade at Camp Dodge, before being posted to a front-line Pioneer Infantry Battalion in [[92nd Infantry Division (United States)|92nd Division]], the "Buffalo Soldiers Division". The 163 BDE was still at Dodge in April 1918.<ref>{{cite web|title=Iowans who served during WWI from North Dakota 'V' |url=https://iagenweb.org/greatwar/mispub/AGND/ND_V.htm |website=The IAGenWeb Project }}</ref>

Upon the end of the war, the post was downsized and turned back over to state authorities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ggarchives.com/Military/WW1/TrainingCamps/CampDodge/index.html|title=Camp Dodge – WW1 Cantonment|website=www.ggarchives.com}}</ref>  Similarly, with the outbreak of the [[Second World War]], Camp Dodge was again handed over to the federal government; however, this time the post was used only as an induction center for new service members.<ref name="auto" />  Camp Dodge has served as a Guard and Reserve installation since the end of the Second World War.
[[File:1918 topographic map of artillery range and Camp Dodge, Iowa Quadrangle Topographical Map, 1918 (cropped).jpg|thumb|1918 [[topographic map]] of artillery range and Camp Dodge, Iowa ]]
During World War II the Camp Dodge was defined as being at the town of Herrold, so many documents reference this name as its post office address. Herrold was surrounded by the camp. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers purchased the town in 1990 to use as a training range.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://archiver.rootsweb.ancestry.com/th/read/IAPOLK/2007-04/1177216437 |title=RootsWeb: IAPOLK-L Re: &#91;IAPOLK&#93; Herrold, Polk County, Iowa |access-date=2014-05-20 |archive-date=2016-03-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305012316/http://archiver.rootsweb.ancestry.com/th/read/IAPOLK/2007-04/1177216437 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The nearby city of Johnston eventually became the new camp address.

Along with the numerous National Guard units located at Camp Dodge, the post is also home to the Sustainment Training Center (formerly the National Maintenance Training Center), Mission Training Complex-Dodge (MTC-Dodge), Joint Forces Headquarters, Iowa's emergency operations center, the operations center for the [[Iowa Communications Network|ICN]], a [[Military Entrance Processing Station|MEPS]] installation, Iowa Law Enforcement Academy, and the State Police academy. The camp is the home of the Iowa Gold Star Military Museum, a member of the Army Museum System.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.history.army.mil/html/museums/dir-links.html |title=Army Museum System |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130821161854/http://www.history.army.mil/html/museums/dir-links.html |archive-date=2013-08-21 |url-status=dead |website=[[United States Army Center of Military History]] }}</ref>
